questions.explanation: R introduces 'the shepherd boys' and the earliest time (morning). Order: R-S-P-Q.

questions.prompt:
The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a paragraph are given. Rearrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the correct order.
S1: Language is more than a means of communication.
P: When a language dies, therefore, a whole way of seeing the world is lost.
Q: It carries the memory, values and knowledge of a people.
R: Unfortunately, many small languages are disappearing as speakers shift to dominant ones.
S: Folk songs, proverbs and names of plants, for example, are passed down only through speech.
S6: Documenting endangered languages is thus an urgent task.
questions.explanation: Q states what language carries; S gives examples; R introduces the decline; P ('therefore') states the loss, leading to the call for action in S6.

questions.prompt:
Rearrange the following sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: When it was finally completed, the bridge cut the journey by two hours.
Q: For years, villagers had to cross the river by boat.
R: During floods, even this became impossible.
S: The government then sanctioned a bridge, which took three years to build.
questions.explanation: Situation (Q) – 'even this' (R) – remedy (S) – 'When it was finally completed' (P).

questions.prompt:
Rearrange the following sentences P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: "Then you must apply for one," said the clerk.
Q: "I would like to open a savings account," said Ravi.
R: "I'm afraid I don't have one," replied Ravi.
S: "Certainly. Do you have an identity proof with your address?" asked the clerk.
questions.explanation: Request (Q) – the clerk's question (S) – Ravi's reply (R) – the clerk's advice (P).

questions.prompt:
The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a paragraph are given. Rearrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the correct order.
S1: Coral reefs are often called the rainforests of the sea.
P: They support an enormous variety of marine life.
Q: Rising sea temperatures, however, are causing corals to lose their colour and die.
R: This process is known as coral bleaching.
S: The Gulf of Mannar has been declared a marine biosphere reserve partly to protect its reefs.
S6: Protecting reefs protects the livelihood of coastal communities too.
questions.explanation: Importance (P) – threat 'however' (Q) – 'This process' named (R) – protective measure (S).

questions.prompt:
The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a paragraph are given. Rearrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the correct order.
S1: Urbanisation is one of the defining trends of the modern era.
P: This influx, in turn, places heavy pressure on housing, transport and water supply.
Q: People migrate from villages to cities in search of jobs and better services.
R: Planners must therefore anticipate growth rather than merely react to it.
S: Where such pressure is ignored, slums and traffic congestion multiply.
S6: Well-planned cities can turn urbanisation into an engine of growth.
questions.explanation: Migration (Q) – 'This influx' (P) – 'such pressure' (S) – 'therefore' the planners' task (R).

questions.prompt:
The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a paragraph are given. Rearrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the correct order.
S1: Scientific knowledge grows through a cycle of observation and testing.
P: The scientist then designs experiments to test it.
Q: An observation that cannot be explained leads to a possible explanation, called a hypothesis.
R: If the results repeatedly support it, the hypothesis gains acceptance as a theory.
S: If they contradict it, the hypothesis is revised or rejected.
S6: In this way, science corrects itself over time.
questions.explanation: Hypothesis (Q) – testing it (P) – 'the results' first named (R) – 'they' (the results) contradict (S).

questions.prompt:
The first (S1) and last (S6) sentences of a paragraph are given. Rearrange the middle sentences P, Q, R and S in the correct order.
S1: The Panchayati Raj system brought democracy to the village level.
P: It gave constitutional status to panchayats.
Q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 was a landmark in this process.
R: It also provided for regular elections and reservation of seats for women.
S: In Tamil Nadu, women's reservation in local bodies has since been raised to fifty per cent.
S6: As a result, lakhs of women now take part in local governance.
questions.explanation: Q names the Act; P ('It') – R ('It also') – S (Tamil Nadu's extension).

questions.prompt: A formal letter begins with the salutation "Dear Sir/Madam". Which complimentary close matches it?
questions.explanation: When the addressee is not named (Dear Sir/Madam), the standard close is 'Yours faithfully'.
questions.trick: Sir/Madam -> faithfully; named person (Dear Mr. Kumar) -> sincerely.

questions.prompt: You begin a formal letter with "Dear Mr. Ramesh". The most appropriate complimentary close is:
questions.explanation: When the addressee is named in the salutation, a formal letter normally closes with 'Yours sincerely'.

questions.prompt: In a letter written to a close friend, which complimentary close is suitable?
questions.explanation: Personal (informal) letters to friends or relatives close with affectionate forms such as 'Yours affectionately' or 'Yours lovingly'.

questions.prompt: In a leave letter written by a student to the Principal, which complimentary close is customarily used in Indian schools?
questions.explanation: Indian school leave letters to the Principal traditionally close with 'Yours obediently' (or 'Your obedient student').

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct order of the parts of a formal letter?
options: Date – Salutation – Sender's address – Subject – Body – Receiver's address – Signature – Complimentary close
Salutation – Subject – Body – Date – Signature – Sender's address – Receiver's address – Complimentary close
Receiver's address – Signature – Subject – Body – Salutation – Date – Sender's address – Complimentary close
Sender's address – Date – Receiver's address – Subject – Salutation – Body – Complimentary close – Signature
questions.explanation: A formal letter opens with the sender's address and date, then the receiver's address, subject and salutation, followed by the body, complimentary close and signature.

questions.prompt: In a formal letter, where is the 'Subject' line placed?
options: After the receiver's address and before the salutation
At the end of the body
questions.explanation: The subject line comes after the inside (receiver's) address and just before the salutation, so the reader knows the purpose at once.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the most suitable subject line for a letter to the Commissioner about irregular garbage collection in your street?
options: Subject: Irregular garbage collection in Gandhi Street, Ward 12
questions.explanation: A subject line should be brief and specific, stating the exact issue and place.

questions.prompt:
Complete the opening of a complaint letter appropriately:
"Sir,
I wish to ______ the poor condition of the road leading to our village school."
questions.explanation: 'I wish to bring to your kind notice...' is the standard formal phrase used to introduce a complaint.

questions.prompt: Choose the most appropriate closing line for a job application letter.
options: I look forward to the opportunity of an interview.
Reply fast or I will apply elsewhere.
questions.explanation: A formal application closes politely by expressing hope for an interview; the other options are rude or casual.

questions.prompt:
Fill in the blank in this leave letter:
"Respected Sir,
As I am suffering from high fever, I am unable to attend school today. ______ grant me leave for two days, i.e., 10th and 11th July."
questions.explanation: 'Kindly grant me leave...' is the polite formal request used in leave letters.

questions.prompt: The abbreviation "Encl." at the foot of a letter indicates that:
options: A copy has been sent to someone else
Some documents are attached with the letter
questions.explanation: 'Encl.' (Enclosure) lists documents attached to the letter.

questions.prompt: "P.S." written after the signature of a letter stands for:
questions.explanation: P.S. (Latin post scriptum) is a note added after the signature.

questions.prompt: In an email, the person whose address is entered in the "Bcc" field:
options: Receives the email, but the other recipients cannot see their address
Is shown to all recipients as the main addressee
questions.explanation: Bcc (blind carbon copy) recipients get the mail while their address stays hidden from the other recipients.

questions.prompt: In the 'Block format' of a formal letter:
options: All parts of the letter begin at the left margin
Every paragraph is indented by five spaces
The address is written in the centre
The signature is written at the top
questions.explanation: In block format, every line, including addresses, date and signature, starts at the left margin with no indentation.

questions.prompt: A letter to the Editor of a newspaper is generally written to:
options: Express a view on a public issue for publication
Invite the editor to a family wedding
questions.explanation: Letters to the Editor raise public issues and seek publication so that the authorities and the public take notice.

questions.prompt: Which salutation is appropriate in a letter to the Editor of a newspaper?
questions.explanation: Letters to the Editor use the formal 'Sir/Madam' (or 'Dear Sir/Madam').

questions.prompt: Which of the following sentences is most suitable for the body of a formal letter?
options: I would be grateful if you could look into this matter at the earliest.
Hey, sort this out quickly, okay?
You people never do anything right.
questions.explanation: Formal letters use polite, complete sentences without slang, abbreviations like 'pls/asap', or accusations.

questions.prompt: The expression "Thanking you in anticipation" in a formal letter means that the writer:
options: Thanks the reader in advance for the action requested
questions.explanation: 'Thanking you in anticipation' thanks the reader beforehand for the help the writer expects.

questions.prompt: A NOTICE is usually written:
options: Inside a box, with a heading, date, clear details and the writer's name and designation
As a long personal letter with a salutation
Only in the form of a poem
questions.explanation: A notice is a short formal announcement, placed in a box, with the institution's name, the word NOTICE, date, heading, body and the issuing authority's signature and designation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following details is LEAST necessary in a school notice announcing an inter-house quiz?
options: Date and time of the quiz
The favourite subject of the person writing the notice
questions.explanation: A notice must answer what, when, where and whom to contact; the writer's personal preferences are irrelevant.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct ending for a notice issued by a school.
questions.explanation: A notice ends with the signature, name and designation of the person issuing it, not with a letter-style complimentary close.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT usually part of an informal letter?
options: A friendly salutation such as 'Dear Priya'
A subject line and the recipient's official designation
questions.explanation: Informal letters do not need a subject line or the recipient's official designation; those belong to formal letters.

questions.prompt: When you write a letter of enquiry to a college asking about admission, the purpose of the letter is to:
options: Seek information about courses, fees and admission procedure
Thank the college for admitting you
questions.explanation: An enquiry letter asks for information.

questions.prompt: Which phrase is most appropriate to introduce enclosed documents in a job application?
options: I'm throwing in my papers, take a look.
Please find enclosed copies of my certificates for your reference.
Certificates are somewhere in this envelope, I think.
Read my certificates if you have time.
questions.explanation: 'Please find enclosed...' is the standard formal way to mention attachments.

questions.prompt:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable phrase:
"Dear Sir,
With reference to your advertisement in The Hindu dated 5th June, ______ the post of Junior Assistant in your office."
options: I order you to give me
questions.explanation: A job application states 'I wish to apply for the post of...' after referring to the advertisement.

questions.prompt: In a business letter, the line "Ref: Your letter No. 245/A2/2024 dated 12.03.2024" is used to:
options: Give the writer's personal phone number
Link the present letter to an earlier letter on the same matter
questions.explanation: A reference line cites earlier correspondence so the reader can trace the file and context.

questions.prompt: Where is the date written in a formal letter in the traditional (semi-block) format used in Indian schools?
options: At the very end of the body
Below the sender's address, before the receiver's address
questions.explanation: The date is written just below the sender's address and before the receiver's (inside) address.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best way to begin the body of a letter to a friend congratulating her on winning a prize?
options: I was thrilled to hear that you won the first prize in the state-level essay competition!
With reference to your letter dated 5th June, I wish to inform you...
I regret to inform you that...
questions.explanation: A congratulatory letter to a friend opens warmly and directly; the others are formal or negative openings.

questions.prompt: A letter written to the Bank Manager requesting a new cheque book is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Letters to officials and institutions for official purposes are formal letters.

questions.prompt: The phrase "I remain" sometimes written before the complimentary close in old-style formal letters is best replaced in modern letters by:
options: Simply writing the complimentary close, e.g., 'Yours faithfully'
questions.explanation: Modern letters avoid old-fashioned phrases like 'I remain' and use just the complimentary close followed by the signature.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that maintains a firm but polite tone in a complaint letter.
options: Your office is completely useless and lazy.
Maybe someday, if you feel like it, you could see the lights.
Despite two earlier complaints, the street lights have not been repaired; I request you to take immediate action.
questions.explanation: A complaint should be firm, factual and courteous, not abusive or vague.

questions.prompt: In an application to the Tahsildar for a community certificate, which closing is appropriate?
questions.explanation: An application to an official ends formally with 'Thanking you, Yours faithfully'.

questions.prompt: An informal letter to your grandfather would begin with the salutation:
questions.explanation: Informal letters to relatives use an affectionate salutation.

questions.prompt: "To whomsoever it may concern" is used as a salutation when:
options: The letter or certificate is meant for any reader and no specific person is addressed
questions.explanation: It is used in certificates and testimonials meant for any authority or reader.

questions.prompt: Which of the following sentences is best suited for the concluding paragraph of an order letter to a book supplier?
options: We hope you are doing well and enjoying the weather.
We are angry about your prices.
Kindly dispatch the books by registered parcel at the earliest and send the bill along with them.
The books may be sent whenever you remember.
questions.explanation: An order letter ends with clear instructions about delivery and payment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is most suitable as the subject line of a leave letter?
options: Sub: Request for leave on 14th and 15th August
Sub: My fever and my grandmother's village
questions.explanation: A subject line states the purpose briefly, specifying the dates of leave.

questions.prompt: In a formal letter, the sender's signature appears:
options: Below the complimentary close, followed by the sender's name
questions.explanation: The signature is placed below 'Yours faithfully/sincerely', with the name written below it.

questions.prompt:
Fill in the blank appropriately:
"I am writing ______ the inconvenience caused to commuters by the frequent cancellation of the 7.30 a.m. bus from Melur to Madurai."
questions.explanation: 'To draw your attention to' is used to introduce a problem in a complaint letter.

questions.prompt:
Complete the letter to the Postmaster:
"Sir,
I had sent a registered parcel to my brother in Delhi on 2nd May. It has not been delivered so far. I request you to ______ and inform me of its present status."
questions.explanation: The writer asks the Postmaster to trace (find out the whereabouts of) the undelivered parcel.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct way to write the receiver's address in a letter to a District Collector?
options: Mr. Collector, Somewhere in the city
questions.explanation: The inside address gives the designation, office, place and PIN code, line by line.

questions.prompt: In a formal email, which is the most suitable subject line for applying for an internship?
options: Application for Summer Internship – B.Com. Student, XYZ College
questions.explanation: A formal email subject is concise and informative; it avoids slang, capitals and exclamation marks.

questions.prompt: "CC" in an official letter or email indicates that:
options: A copy of the letter is being sent to the persons named
The writer has changed their address
questions.explanation: 'CC' (carbon copy / courtesy copy) lists others to whom copies are sent for information.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the most appropriate first sentence of a letter of apology to a customer for a delayed delivery?
options: Delays happen, so do not worry about it.
We sincerely apologise for the delay in delivering your order No. 1452.
You ordered too late, so it is your fault.
We are pleased to announce our new products.
questions.explanation: An apology letter begins by acknowledging the problem and apologising clearly.

questions.prompt: A student writes: "Respected Madam, I request you to issue my Transfer Certificate as my father has been transferred to Salem." Which part of the letter is this?
questions.explanation: Stating the request and its reason forms the body of the letter.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of an informal expression that should be avoided in a formal letter?
options: "I shall be grateful for your kind consideration."
"I request you to look into the matter."
questions.explanation: Slang such as 'thanks a ton, buddy' is not suitable in formal correspondence.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence in an invitation letter:
"The Headmaster and staff of Government Higher Secondary School, Vellore, request the pleasure of your ______ at the Annual Day celebrations on 20th January at 5 p.m."
questions.explanation: Formal invitations use the fixed phrase 'request the pleasure of your company'.

questions.prompt: "R.S.V.P." printed on an invitation card means:
questions.explanation: R.S.V.P. is from French 'Répondez s'il vous plaît', meaning 'please reply'.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a 'formal invitation' written in the third person?
options: I am inviting you to my sister's wedding, please come.
Mr. and Mrs. K. Raman request the pleasure of your company at the wedding of their daughter...
Hey! Wedding next week, don't miss it.
You must come to our wedding without fail, dear.
questions.explanation: Formal invitations are written in the third person ('Mr. and Mrs. ... request...'), without a salutation or signature.

questions.prompt: A reply to a formal invitation, declining it, should:
options: Criticise the host's choice of date
Thank the host, express regret and give a brief reason
Ask the host to postpone the function
questions.explanation: A polite refusal thanks the host, regrets inability to attend and gives a short reason.

questions.prompt: Which of the following closing sentences is appropriate for a letter requesting a refund?
options: Keep the money, I don't care.
I request you to refund the amount of Rs. 1,250 to my account at the earliest.
questions.explanation: A refund request ends with a clear, polite statement of the action and amount expected.

questions.prompt: A letter of complaint to a company about a defective product should ideally include:
options: The date of purchase, bill number and the nature of the defect
A list of other companies' prices only
questions.explanation: Specific details such as date, bill/invoice number and the defect help the company act quickly.

questions.prompt:
In the letter below, choose the most suitable phrase for the blank.
"Sir,
I am a resident of Anna Nagar. ______, the drainage in our street has been overflowing, causing a health hazard."
questions.explanation: The complaint describes a continuing problem, so a duration phrase ('For the past two weeks') with the present perfect continuous is correct.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct format of the date in a formal letter written in Indian/British style?
questions.explanation: Indian/British style writes the day first: '15th August 2024' or '15.08.2024'.

questions.prompt: Which of these sentences would be appropriate in a personal letter but NOT in an official letter?
options: Mom sends her love and asks when you'll visit us next.
I request you to issue a duplicate mark sheet.
The fee of Rs. 200 has been remitted by demand draft.
Kindly acknowledge receipt of the documents.
questions.explanation: References to family affection belong to personal letters; the others are official in content and tone.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the most suitable salutation for a letter addressed to 'The Manager, State Bank of India, Madurai'?
questions.explanation: A letter to an official whose name is not known uses 'Sir/Madam'.

questions.prompt: While writing a formal letter, the main body should ideally be divided into:
options: A poem followed by the signature
An opening paragraph stating the purpose, a middle with details, and a closing paragraph with the request or action expected
questions.explanation: A clear three-part structure (purpose, details, action) makes a formal letter easy to follow.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Every evening, long queues form outside the ration shop in our street. Many people leave without their rice because the stock runs out before their turn.
Which inference is best supported?
options: People in the street do not eat rice
The supply of rice at the shop is not enough for the demand
The ration shop is open only on Sundays
Rice prices in the market have fallen
questions.explanation: Stock running out while people are still waiting shows that supply falls short of demand.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The temple car festival in the town drew lakhs of devotees. Special buses were run from neighbouring districts, and all lodges in the town were full a week in advance.
What can be inferred?
options: Only local residents attend the festival
The festival attracts visitors from well beyond the town
Buses do not run to the town on other days
questions.explanation: Special buses from other districts and fully booked lodges indicate many outside visitors.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Selvi's mother noticed that Selvi had stopped playing outdoors, kept rubbing her eyes and held her books very close to her face while reading.
What is the most reasonable inference?
options: Selvi may have a problem with her eyesight
Selvi is preparing for a sports event
Selvi's books are printed in large letters
questions.explanation: Rubbing the eyes and holding books very close are common signs of poor vision.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: In the last ten years, the number of sparrows seen in the city has dropped sharply. During the same period, old tiled houses with open eaves have been replaced by sealed concrete buildings.
Which inference is most reasonable?
options: Loss of nesting places may be one reason for the decline of sparrows
Sparrows have increased in the city
questions.explanation: The passage links the decline with the disappearance of open eaves where sparrows nest; it suggests a possible cause, not a proven one.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The shopkeeper said, "Sorry, we have sold the last umbrella. Come back on Monday; a fresh stock is expected."
Which of the following can be inferred?
options: Monday is a holiday for the shop
Umbrellas are in high demand at present
questions.explanation: The stock is sold out, which implies strong demand; nothing suggests the shop is closed on Monday.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: There were different streams in the Indian freedom movement – moderates, extremists, revolutionaries and socialists – each with its own methods.
Which is the best inference?
options: All freedom fighters followed a single method
The freedom movement had no leaders
The Indian freedom movement was not uniform in its approach
questions.explanation: Several streams with different methods mean the movement was diverse (heterogeneous), not uniform.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Although the factory has installed new machines, its output has not increased. Workers say they were never trained to operate them.
What can be inferred?
options: Lack of training may be preventing the new machines from being used effectively
The new machines are of poor quality
The workers do not want to work
questions.explanation: The passage gives the workers' lack of training as the explanation; nothing is said about the machines' quality.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: When the teacher entered the classroom, the noise stopped at once and all the students stood up.
Which inference is best?
questions.explanation: Falling silent and standing up show respect for the teacher.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Kumaran has been late to office four times this week. Each time, he blamed traffic. His colleagues who travel by the same route reached on time.
What is the most reasonable inference?
options: Traffic on the route is always heavy
Traffic may not be the real reason for Kumaran's late arrival
Kumaran's colleagues live in the office
questions.explanation: Others on the same route arrived on time, so his excuse is doubtful.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: All the students who scored above 90 in the test were given a medal. Divya was not given a medal.
Which conclusion follows definitely?
options: Divya did not write the test
questions.explanation: If every student above 90 got a medal and Divya did not, she could not have scored above 90. Whether she failed or scored exactly 90 cannot be known.
questions.trick: Only the statement guaranteed by the premises 'follows definitely'.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Some engineers are poets. All poets are good speakers.
Which conclusion follows?
options: No engineer is a good speaker
questions.explanation: The engineers who are poets must be good speakers, so 'some engineers are good speakers' follows.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The pond near the village used to dry up every April. Since the villagers desilted it last year and cleared the channels that feed it, it has held water through the summer.
What can be inferred?
options: Desilting and clearing the feeder channels improved the pond's water storage
The villagers built a new pond
The pond now dries up in March
questions.explanation: The change followed desilting and clearing of channels, suggesting they increased storage and inflow.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Reforestation projects restore degraded ecosystems. They increase biodiversity and improve air quality. They also enhance water retention.
Which set of statements best supports the claim that reforestation is beneficial?
(a) Reforestation decreases biodiversity.
(b) Reforestation restores degraded ecosystems.
(c) Reforestation improves air quality.
(d) Reforestation enhances water retention.
questions.explanation: Statement (a) contradicts the passage; (b), (c) and (d) are all benefits stated in it.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: First, the paddy is harvested. Then it is threshed to separate the grain. Next, the grain is dried in the sun. Finally, it is husked to obtain rice.
Which statements correctly describe the sequence?
(a) Threshing comes before drying.
(b) Husking comes before harvesting.
(c) Drying comes after threshing and before husking.
(d) The process begins with husking.
questions.explanation: Order: harvest – thresh – dry – husk. Only (a) and (c) agree with it.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Online shopping and traditional shopping both let customers buy goods. Online shopping offers home delivery and wider choice, while traditional shopping lets customers touch and examine goods before buying.
Which statements correctly compare the two?
(a) Both allow customers to buy goods.
(b) Only traditional shopping offers home delivery.
(c) Traditional shopping allows customers to examine goods physically.
(d) Online shopping offers a narrower choice.
questions.explanation: The passage says both allow buying and only traditional shopping allows physical examination; (b) and (d) reverse the facts.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The library's new rule allows students to borrow books only if they have returned all earlier books. Arjun borrowed two books yesterday.
What can be inferred?
options: Arjun had no overdue books when he borrowed them
Arjun has lost a library book
The library has stopped lending books
questions.explanation: Under the rule, borrowing is possible only after returning earlier books, so Arjun must have had none pending.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The speaker paused, looked at his watch, and said, "I will be brief." He then spoke for an hour.
What does the writer most likely imply?
options: The speaker did not keep his promise to be brief
The audience asked him to continue
The speech lasted only a few minutes
questions.explanation: The contrast between 'I will be brief' and speaking for an hour is ironic: he did not keep his word.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Many coastal villages that had dense mangrove forests suffered less damage in the 2004 tsunami than nearby villages without them.
Which inference is best supported?
options: Villages without mangroves were not affected at all
Mangrove forests can reduce the impact of waves on the coast
Mangroves grow only after a tsunami
questions.explanation: The comparison suggests mangroves acted as a buffer against the waves.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The new bus route was introduced in January. Since then, the number of students attending the village high school has risen, especially among girls from distant hamlets.
What is the most reasonable inference?
options: Girls do not like the school
The school has shifted to the town
Easier transport has helped more students, especially girls, attend school
Fewer buses run now than before
questions.explanation: Attendance rose after the bus route started, especially among those who live far away.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: "The Collector ordered the immediate closure of the quarry after residents complained that blasting had cracked the walls of their houses."
Which inference can be drawn?
options: The Collector treated the residents' complaint as serious
The quarry was closed before the complaint
The houses were built by the quarry owners
questions.explanation: Ordering immediate closure in response to the complaint shows that it was taken seriously.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The match was to begin at 3 p.m. At 2.55 p.m., dark clouds gathered, the umpires inspected the pitch, and the ground staff rushed out with covers.
What can be inferred?
options: Rain was expected to interrupt the match
questions.explanation: Dark clouds and covers being brought out indicate expected rain.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Every candidate who passed the written test was called for the interview. Nirmala was called for the interview.
Which conclusion is valid?
options: None of the given conclusions follows definitely
Only Nirmala was called for the interview
questions.explanation: The statement says passing leads to an interview call, but it does not say only those who passed were called; so we cannot be sure Nirmala passed.
questions.trick: 'All A are B' does not mean 'all B are A'.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The price of onions doubled in a single month after unseasonal rains damaged the crop in the major growing districts.
Which inference is best supported?
options: A fall in supply due to crop damage pushed up onion prices
Onions are not grown in India
questions.explanation: Crop damage reduced supply, which explains the price rise.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The author writes, "My grandfather never went to school, yet he could calculate the yield of his field to the last measure and predict rain from the behaviour of ants."
What does the author most likely want to convey?
options: Practical knowledge can be gained without formal schooling
His grandfather was a weather scientist
questions.explanation: The 'never went to school, yet...' contrast highlights his practical wisdom; it does not argue that schools are useless.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: In a survey, 80% of the people who used the new park said they felt healthier. The survey did not include people who did not use the park.
Which statement is the most reasonable?
options: The park definitely makes everyone healthier
People who avoid the park are unhealthy
Only 20% of the town is healthy
The survey alone cannot prove that the park made people healthier
questions.explanation: Without comparing with non-users, the survey cannot establish cause and effect.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The old banyan tree in the village square has been the meeting place of the village elders for generations. When the road-widening plan proposed cutting it down, the villagers submitted a petition with five hundred signatures.
What can be inferred?
options: The villagers support cutting the tree
The tree was planted last year
The villagers value the tree and want it preserved
The road has already been widened
questions.explanation: A large petition against cutting the tree shows their attachment to it.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Of the 40 students in the class, 25 play cricket and 20 play football. Every student plays at least one of the two games.
Which conclusion follows?
options: At least 5 students play both games
Football is more popular than cricket
questions.explanation: 25 + 20 = 45 exceeds 40, so at least 45 – 40 = 5 students play both; with 'every student plays at least one', exactly 5 play both.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: The doctor said, "Your test results are normal, but I would like you to cut down on salt and walk every day."

options: The doctor is recommending precautions to stay healthy
questions.explanation: Normal results plus lifestyle advice indicate preventive care, not illness.

questions.prompt:

Which inference is most reasonable?
options: Clearing encroachments on inlet channels could help the tanks fill
questions.explanation: The passage blames blocked inlets, not lack of rain, for the dry tanks.

questions.prompt:
Read the passage and choose the best inference.
Passage: Crypto-currencies and stocks both involve investment. Crypto-currencies are highly volatile, while stocks are relatively stable. Both are affected by market fluctuations, though differently.
Which statements accurately compare them?
(a) Neither involves investment.
(b) Both involve investment.
(c) Both are immune to market fluctuations.
(d) They react differently to market fluctuations.
questions.explanation: The passage states both involve investment and react differently to fluctuations; (a) and (c) contradict it.

questions.prompt:

options: He also did small jobs for neighbours to earn extra money.
He spent all his money on sweets.
He decided he did not want a bicycle.
His bicycle was stolen the next day.
questions.explanation: The blank must add to his saving effort and lead to having 'enough' money.

options: Many trees are cut down for furniture.
They give out oxygen and absorb carbon dioxide.
Trees cannot grow in cities at all.
Some people are afraid of climbing trees.
questions.explanation: The paragraph lists benefits; 'They also provide...' needs a preceding benefit.

options: The road to the town was closed last year.
Many families moved away from the village.
Doctors in the town went on leave.
Last year, a primary health centre was opened in the village.
questions.explanation: 'Since then' needs an event that explains the increase in safe deliveries.

Choose the sentence that best fills the blank in the paragraph.

options: Therefore, everyone should use them all day.
However, they must be used in moderation.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes harm, so the blank needs a contrast ('However') introducing caution.

He compared the two kinds of speech to fruit.
He was born in a palace in Rome.
He disliked all kinds of fruit.
questions.explanation: The blank introduces the comparison that the following sentence explains (Kural 100).

Students were told to bring plastic bags.
The drive was cancelled after one day.
Dustbins were checked every week to see how much plastic was being thrown away.
questions.explanation: The blank must be consistent with the drive and its success.

questions.prompt:

In reality, hard work and preparation matter far more.
Harvests do not depend on anything.
questions.explanation: The example of the farmer supports the idea that preparation matters more than luck.

The hall was ready a day early.
questions.explanation: 'As a result' requires a cause for the delay.

They are always more expensive than imported fruits.
They are also rich in the nutrients our bodies need in that season.
They are not grown in India.
questions.explanation: The blank continues the list of advantages of seasonal fruits; the other options contradict the first sentence.

he refused to look at the water.
he complained that the beach was boring.
he fell asleep in the car.

Elderly people could call it for medical, legal or emotional help.
Senior citizens were not allowed to use it.
It worked only for one day.

options: Firstly, newspapers are printed on paper.
Secondly, it improves our vocabulary and language.
questions.explanation: The paragraph lists benefits in order; the blank is the second benefit before 'Finally'.

The engineers were dismissed for raising the alarm.

Paragraph: Hard water does not lather easily with soap. ______ Such water also leaves white deposits in kettles and pipes.

This is why it is used in batteries.
It is always found in rainwater.
This is because it contains dissolved salts of calcium and magnesium.

options: It is a waste of paper.
It allows us to express our feelings freely.
It is useful only for famous people.
questions.explanation: 'It also helps...' requires a preceding benefit.

questions.prompt:
Choose the sentence that best fills the blank in the paragraph.
Paragraph: Many young people leave villages to work in cities. ______ As a result, agricultural work in some villages now suffers from a shortage of labour.
options: Cities have no jobs at all.
They are attracted by better wages and facilities in urban areas.
Village wages are higher than city wages.
They prefer farming to every other job.

Choose the sentence that best fills the blank in the paragraph.
Paragraph: Mahatma Gandhi believed in non-violence. ______ He led millions in peaceful protests such as the Salt Satyagraha.

He disliked all forms of protest.
He held that even the strongest opponent could be won over through truth and love.
He never took part in the freedom struggle.

Paragraph: Arun forgot to switch off the geyser before leaving for college. ______ He decided to be more careful in future.

He never used the geyser at all.
His college gave him a prize for the geyser.
When he returned, his mother told him about the high electricity bill and the risk of overheating.
questions.explanation: The blank must show a consequence that leads to his resolution to be careful.

questions.prompt:
Choose the sentence that best fills the blank in the paragraph.
Paragraph: The Western Ghats receive heavy rainfall during the south-west monsoon. ______ The eastern side, lying in the rain-shadow, receives much less rain at that time.

The eastern slopes receive the heaviest rain.
The monsoon winds blow from the east.

She forgot every word and stopped singing.

Everyone agrees that examinations are perfect.
Memory is never needed in life.
questions.explanation: The blank explains the first view; 'Others feel' presents the opposite view.

They are cheaper than all other vehicles.

questions.prompt:
Choose the correct set of words to fill the blanks in order:

questions.explanation: Heavy flooding rain is torrential; sharing shows a generous child; a hard-to-follow path is winding; an annoying short reply is curt.

4. The ______ fragrance of jasmine filled the room.
questions.explanation: New vaccine – pioneering research; cannot climb – frail; satisfies no one – vague; jasmine – sweet fragrance.

It will be rejected for being late
It will be returned for completion
It will be kept for next year

Because the road is under repair

The animals bite visitors who feed them
